public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data centers aren't getting finished; OpenAI and Anthropic make up 75% or more of all AI compute capacity and more than 50% of Amazon, Google and Microsoft's revenue backlog; and both are horrendously unprofitable apart from brazen accounting tricks.

statement.excerpt: Don’t worry about the fact that data centers aren’t getting finished, or that OpenAI and Anthropic make up 75%+ of all AI compute capacity, or that they make up more than 50% of Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s revenue backlog, or that both of them are horrendously unprofitable outside of brazen accounting tricks that would only work on a business and tech media intent on believing everything they say.

from_speaker: more than 50% of Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s revenue backlog
both of them are horrendously unprofitable
our_interpretation: The construction clause means material delivery problems, not that no data center anywhere is completed.
All AI compute capacity means worldwide operational AI computing capacity, including capacity used internally by other developers; announced future capacity is excluded.
The backlog clause is read as the two customers' combined share of the three named providers' combined backlog. A separate-provider reading remains possible.
The target period is January–March 2026, the latest completed quarterly reporting period before the post; backlog and capacity are stocks at that period's end.
Unprofitable ordinarily concerns company-wide losses, but the speaker does not specify net income, operating income, cash burn, or an accounting basis.
Accounting tricks requires evidence of materially misleading accounting treatment; the existence of disclosed adjustments alone is insufficient.

The single metric_scope object records the backlog-share assertion. The separate profitability assertion concerns a flow with an unspecified measure and basis and cannot be combined with that stock measure for a definitive score.
criteria.support_condition: Matching-period construction records show material delivery failures; a worldwide capacity inventory establishes at least 75%; comparable customer-level backlog records establish more than 50% for the named providers; and comparable accounts establish substantial losses and materially misleading accounting treatment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matching-scope evidence establishes that one or more specified thresholds or factual components are false. A different provider set, future capacity commitments, or a different profit measure cannot establish contradiction.

evidence.locator: Opening analysis, paragraph describing the 2026 project pipeline
evidence.explanation: The tracker documents a substantial pipeline without visible construction progress. That supports concern about delivery, but projects awaiting future completion dates are not yet demonstrated failures to finish.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood's prepared remarks, commercial results
evidence.explanation: Microsoft distinguishes backlog growth with and without OpenAI. This one-provider growth measure does not establish the two customers' share of the three named providers' combined backlog.

evidence.publisher: Anthropic, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: Anthropic's filing acknowledges historical net losses. Its broader reporting period, single-company scope, and distinction between accounting measures prevent it from settling the March-quarter assertion about both companies or alleged misleading accounting.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A target-period worldwide compute inventory, customer-level backlog reconciliation for Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, dated construction-delivery records, and comparable financial accounts with a specified profit measure and evidence addressing the alleged accounting treatment.
